## Concept in detail — expanded study notes
A stock balance describes recorded movements, not crop health. Keep the unit consistent: sacks cannot be added to kilograms without a measured conversion. A sack count also says nothing about moisture or quality.

## Terms and distinctions — expanded study notes
Use a movement ledger with date, reference, incoming sacks, outgoing sacks and running balance. Physical count is a separate observation. A discrepancy is the difference between recorded balance and counted stock; its cause remains unverified.

## A repeatable method — expanded study notes
Reconcile in order: check opening stock, match dispatch references, match receipts, then repeat the physical count. Record corrections as new entries with reasons rather than rewriting the original record.

## Step-by-step walkthrough — expanded study notes
Start at 80; subtract 25 to reach 55; add 10 to reach 65. Compare 62 counted with 65 recorded: counted minus recorded is -3. Ask whether a receipt was duplicated or a dispatch omitted; neither is established by the difference.

Separate a trigger from an action. Receiving an appointment event is permission to prepare the configured draft, not permission to send any generated message. Put approval between generation and the external action.

## Concept in detail — expanded study notes
An assistive rule can identify records for review without deciding guilt, creditworthiness or eligibility. This exercise uses a fictional threshold, not a real banking requirement. State the limited purpose alongside the result.

## Terms and distinctions — expanded study notes
Strictly above means greater than, not greater than or equal to. Store amounts with their currency and preserve exact monetary values. An empty amount is unknown, not zero, and requires a separate handling rule.

## A repeatable method — expanded study notes
Define three outcomes: matches rule, does not match rule and insufficient data. Test just below, exactly at and just above the boundary. Keep human review separate from the mechanical comparison.

Compare 8,000 > 10,000: false; 12,000 > 10,000: true; 10,000 > 10,000: false. The review list contains only the second record. Label the output 'fictional threshold matches' rather than 'fraudulent transfers'.

## Concept in detail — expanded study notes
Customer compliments, repeat requests and payment are different evidence. Define the hypothesis before interviewing: for example, shops will pay for reviewed descriptions because it reduces preparation effort. A hypothesis remains uncertain until tested.

## Terms and distinctions — expanded study notes
A funnel counts movement through specified stages. In this case, liking, requesting and buying are observations; do not assume they form nested stages unless participant-level records show that relationship.

## A repeatable method — expanded study notes
Design a pilot offer with a fixed deliverable, price, review responsibility and cancellation terms. Track effort per shop and the number returning for a second paid order. Use fictional interviews for class practice.

## Step-by-step walkthrough — expanded study notes
Ten shops tried the sample and one bought: observed sample-to-pilot purchase rate is 1/10 = 10%. Six positive comments give a separate 60% positive-response figure. Neither rate establishes repeat demand or profit.

## Concept in detail — expanded study notes
An editorial brief states audience, purpose, source facts and the action readers should take. Repurposing changes presentation while preserving the evidence. Do not turn a modest participation result into a stronger outcome claim.

## Terms and distinctions — expanded study notes
Attendance counts people present; submission counts completed work received. A submission rate needs a denominator and time window. Employment is a separate outcome requiring separate evidence.

## A repeatable method — expanded study notes
Write a facts ledger first: 24 attended; 18 submitted; later employment was not measured. Draft a report sentence, a caption and a spoken script from that ledger, then check each claim against it.

## Step-by-step walkthrough — expanded study notes
Calculate 18 divided by 24 = 0.75, or 75%. Report: 'Eighteen of 24 attendees submitted practice work.' Caption: 'Practice continued after the workshop: 18 submissions from 24 attendees.' Neither implies job placement.

## Concept in detail — expanded study notes
A service response should resolve the customer's actual issue under the applicable policy. Different policy clauses can govern different circumstances. Opening a damaged book does not automatically turn a damaged-delivery case into an ordinary return.

## Terms and distinctions — expanded study notes
Separate acknowledgement, information request, routing and decision. Acknowledging a complaint does not approve a refund. Ask only for the approved minimum reference needed to locate the order.

## A repeatable method — expanded study notes
Map the ticket to the damaged-delivery branch. Draft an acknowledgement, request the permitted order reference and explain supervisor review. Do not invent a refund deadline or guarantee the outcome.

## Step-by-step walkthrough — expanded study notes
Draft: 'I am sorry the book arrived with torn pages. Please provide your order reference through the approved support channel so a supervisor can review the damaged delivery.' This routes the case without deciding it.

## Concept in detail — expanded study notes
A resolved flag can measure agent closure rather than a lasting solution. Define the review window, reopening rules and case unit before comparing performance. Fast closure is not enough if the same issue repeatedly returns.

## Terms and distinctions — expanded study notes
Initial resolution rate uses initially closed cases divided by all cases. Sustained resolution within this exercise subtracts reopened cases from those initially closed. Both rates must use the same observation window.

## A repeatable method — expanded study notes
Build a case ledger containing case ID, initial closure, reopening and final observed state. Reconcile aggregate counts to individual records and check that a reopened case is not counted twice.

## Step-by-step walkthrough — expanded study notes
Out of 100 cases, 80 initially close. Twenty of those reopen, leaving 60 sustained closures in the window. Report initial closure 80%, sustained closure 60%, and reopening among initial closures 20/80 = 25%.

A strong CV bullet links an action to genuine evidence. Quantities can describe scope, such as three events, without inventing an impact measure. Plain accurate wording is better than impressive claims you cannot defend.

## Concept in detail — expanded study notes
Start with the question, not the chart. 'How many attendees passed?' differs from 'How many registrants have a recorded pass?' The data grain is one learner's workshop record, and each calculation must respect it.

## Terms and distinctions — expanded study notes
Missing, zero and failure are different values. An absent learner with no score has no observed test result. Create separate attendance and outcome fields so missing assessment data is not silently converted into failure.

## A repeatable method — expanded study notes
List the four records and filter attendees before calculating attendee pass rate. For registration coverage, use all registrants. Label both denominators and show missing-score count separately.

Attendees are A, B and C; A and B passed. Compute 2/3 = 66.7%. All registrants are A–D, so recorded passes per registrant are 2/4 = 50%. D remains absent with an unknown test result.

## Concept in detail — expanded study notes
A join connects rows according to matching keys. It can multiply records when the relationship is one-to-many or many-to-many. Decide whether your output represents one order, one customer or one contact before joining.

## Terms and distinctions — expanded study notes
Grain means what one row represents. A unique customer key in Orders is not guaranteed: one customer can place several orders. Likewise, Contacts may contain several contact methods, each valid but unsuitable for direct revenue summation.

## A repeatable method — expanded study notes
Count rows and total revenue before the join. Examine key uniqueness in each table. Choose a primary contact by an explicit rule, or aggregate orders separately and present contacts without summing duplicated amounts.

## Step-by-step walkthrough — expanded study notes
Orders 100 and 200 each match two contact rows. The result contains 100, 100, 200, 200, totaling 600. The original revenue remains 300. Deduplicating by amount alone is unsafe because distinct real orders can share an amount.

## Concept in detail — expanded study notes
An education pilot includes teaching, content, access and assessment conditions. A score difference may reflect any of these. Define the learning goal and what evidence would count as improvement before choosing an AI tool.

## Concept in detail — expanded study notes
A pilot tests a narrow business proposition with limited evidence. Keep revenue, direct delivery costs and fixed costs separate. A small positive remainder does not prove that the business can acquire and retain customers at scale.

## Terms and distinctions — expanded study notes
Revenue is price times paid units. Contribution subtracts stated direct costs. The remainder after stated fixed costs is a simplified result, not a complete accounting profit; omitted costs must be identified.

## A repeatable method — expanded study notes
Create a transparent worksheet with price, paying users, direct costs and fixed costs. Vary one assumption at a time. Explain whether direct costs remain fixed in the scenario or change with customer count.

## Step-by-step walkthrough — expanded study notes
Five payments of 500 produce 2,500. Subtract 1,500 to get contribution 1,000; subtract 800 to leave 200. Under a scenario with the same stated costs and only four payments, the remainder is -300.

## Concept in detail — expanded study notes
A scenario model expresses assumptions, calculations and outputs. AI can draft a narrative, but formulas and reconciled inputs determine the result. Keep this classroom exercise distinct from advice about actual investments or financial decisions.

## Terms and distinctions — expanded study notes
A percentage change uses a specified base. Ten percent of 12,000 is 1,200. Holding costs unchanged is an assumption, not a general rule about how a business behaves when revenue falls.

## A repeatable method — expanded study notes
Write the equation surplus = revenue - variable costs - fixed costs. Place assumptions in labelled cells. Recalculate the base and changed scenario manually before accepting any generated commentary.

## Step-by-step walkthrough — expanded study notes
Base: 12,000 - 7,000 - 3,000 = 2,000. Lower revenue: 12,000 × 0.90 = 10,800. With the exercise costs unchanged, 10,800 - 10,000 = 800. The surplus falls 1,200, or 60% of its original value.

## Concept in detail — expanded study notes
A useful business calculation starts with a clearly bounded offer. State what the customer receives, who reviews it and what counts as completion. Demand testing and cost calculations answer different questions and both are needed.

## Terms and distinctions — expanded study notes
Contribution per order is selling price minus the stated variable cost. Break-even in this simplified exercise is fixed cost divided by positive contribution. A nonpositive contribution cannot cover fixed costs by selling more identical units.

## A repeatable method — expanded study notes
Calculate contribution, then the number of whole orders needed to cover fixed cost. If the division is fractional, round up for whole orders. List omitted costs instead of hiding them inside an optimistic result.

## Step-by-step walkthrough — expanded study notes
At 300 price and 120 variable cost, contribution is 180. Divide fixed cost 1,800 by 180 to get ten orders. Nine orders contribute 1,620 and leave a 180 shortfall; ten cover only the stated costs.
